uncited: An out-of-core iso-surface ray tracing engine designed to render volume datasets exceeding single-machine main memory limits by leveraging a PC cluster.
It employs a hierarchical grid acceleration structure with a three-level bricking approach to minimize memory overhead, enabling interactive frame rates for terabyte-scale data.

It differs from its parent [Ray-marching reference (min-max octree accelerated)](1554-ray-marching-reference-min-max-octree-accelerated.md) by using a rectilinear hierarchical grid instead of an octree, and from [Object-Order Iso-Surface Rendering with Macro-Cells](1757-object-order-iso-surface-rendering-with-macro-cells.md) by relying on image-order ray traversal and distributed out-of-core data loading rather than object-order macro-cell processing.
- Volume dataset $V$ with dimensions $D_x \times D_y \times D_z$ and voxel resolution.
- Camera parameters (origin $\mathbf{o}$, direction $\mathbf{d}$).
- Cluster configuration (number of nodes, network topology).
- Rendered image tiles distributed across cluster nodes.
-   Leaf level: Macro-cells of size $8^3$ voxels.
-   Internal nodes: Store min/max scalar values of their children.
-   Local memory cache on each cluster node.
-   Stores loaded voxel bricks (sub-volumes) requested by rays.
-   Master node divides the image into rectangular tiles.
-   Tiles are distributed to render nodes.
-   Start at the top level of the hierarchical grid.
-   **Empty Space Skipping:** Check the min/max values stored in the current node.
-   At the leaf level, the ray intersects a brick of $8^3$ voxels.
-   Perform analytic iso-surface intersection tests within the voxel grid.
Cardano's formula provides the exact roots.
-   Request the brick from the DataServer.
-   DataServer loads the brick from the network storage if not in memory.
-   Compute shading and color at intersection points.
-   Accumulate results into the image tile buffer.
-   **Time Complexity:** Depends on the number of macro-cells traversed.
Empty space skipping reduces average case complexity.
DataServer cache size depends on working set of bricks.
-   Handles datasets too large for single-machine memory.
-   Low memory overhead for acceleration structure.
-   **When to use:** Large-scale scientific visualization where data exceeds single-node memory and cluster resources are available.
Extended to out-of-core rendering on PC clusters.
